questions.stem: Metals conduct electricity in the solid state because they contain

options.text: mobile ions
delocalised electrons
shared electron pairs
hydrogen bonds

questions.explanation: In a metal the outer electrons leave the individual atoms and form a sea of delocalised electrons around the positive ion lattice. When a potential difference is applied these electrons drift towards the positive terminal, carrying current, while the ions themselves stay in place.

distractorRationale.a: The metal ions are fixed in the lattice; mobile ions are how molten ionic compounds conduct
distractorRationale.c: Shared pairs are localised between two atoms and cannot move through the structure
distractorRationale.d: Hydrogen bonds are attractions between molecules and carry no charge

questions.stem: Copper can be hammered into sheets without shattering, whereas a crystal of sodium chloride crumbles. This is because in copper

options.text: the bonds are much weaker, so the metal gives way easily
layers of ions can slide over one another while the electron sea maintains the bonding
the atoms are not bonded to each other at all
the atoms are arranged randomly rather than in a lattice

questions.explanation: When a metal is struck, planes of positive ions slip past one another, but every ion remains embedded in the same delocalised electron sea, so the attraction is unbroken and the metal simply changes shape. In sodium chloride the same slip brings like charges face to face, and the resulting repulsion splits the crystal.

distractorRationale.a: Metallic bonding is strong, which is why most metals have high melting points
distractorRationale.c: Copper atoms are firmly bonded; an unbonded solid would not exist
distractorRationale.d: Metals are crystalline with regular close-packed lattices

questions.stem: Hydrogen bonding occurs in a compound when hydrogen is directly bonded to

options.text: carbon, silicon or sulphur
fluorine, oxygen or nitrogen
any non-metal
sodium, potassium or calcium

questions.explanation: Hydrogen bonding needs a very electronegative, very small atom so that the hydrogen is left with a large partial positive charge and the partner atom carries an accessible lone pair. Only fluorine, oxygen and nitrogen meet both conditions, which is why HF, H2O and NH3 boil far higher than expected.

distractorRationale.a: Carbon, silicon and sulphur are too weakly electronegative to polarise the H atom sufficiently
distractorRationale.c: Chlorine, for example, is electronegative but too large, so HCl has only dipole-dipole attraction
distractorRationale.d: These are metals; hydrogen combines with them to form ionic hydrides, not hydrogen-bonded molecules

options.text: water molecules lose mass on freezing
hydrogen bonds hold the molecules in an open lattice, so ice is less dense than liquid water
air is trapped inside every ice crystal
the covalent bonds in ice are longer than those in liquid water

questions.explanation: In ice each water molecule forms four hydrogen bonds arranged tetrahedrally, which locks the molecules into a rigid, open, cage-like structure containing large empty spaces. That structure occupies more volume for the same mass than liquid water, so the density of ice is lower and it floats.

distractorRationale.a: Mass is conserved when water freezes; only volume changes
distractorRationale.c: Pure ice made from degassed water still floats, so trapped air is not the cause
distractorRationale.d: The O-H covalent bond length is essentially the same; it is the spacing between molecules that changes

questions.stem: The boiling points of the halogens increase from fluorine to iodine because

options.text: the covalent bond within each molecule becomes stronger
van der Waals forces between molecules increase as the molecules get larger
hydrogen bonding becomes possible in the larger halogens
electronegativity increases down the group

questions.explanation: Halogen molecules are non-polar, so the only attraction between them is the van der Waals force. Larger molecules have more electrons and a more easily distorted electron cloud, producing stronger temporary dipoles, so more energy is needed to separate the molecules and the boiling point rises.

distractorRationale.a: The X-X bond actually gets weaker down the group, and in any case it is not broken during boiling
distractorRationale.c: The halogens contain no hydrogen, so hydrogen bonding is impossible
distractorRationale.d: Electronegativity decreases down the group and does not determine boiling point for non-polar molecules

questions.stem: Magnesium has a much higher melting point than sodium mainly because

options.text: magnesium atoms are much larger than sodium atoms
magnesium contributes two electrons per atom to the electron sea and forms a 2+ ion
magnesium forms covalent bonds while sodium forms metallic bonds
magnesium has more neutrons in its nucleus

questions.explanation: Metallic bond strength depends on the charge density of the ion and the number of delocalised electrons. Magnesium releases two electrons per atom rather than one and forms a smaller, doubly charged Mg2+ ion, so the attraction between the lattice and the electron sea is far stronger and much more energy is needed to melt it.

distractorRationale.a: Magnesium atoms are smaller than sodium atoms, which strengthens rather than weakens the bonding
distractorRationale.c: Both elements are metals with metallic bonding
distractorRationale.d: Neutron number affects mass but not the strength of the metallic bond
